# Psalm 27 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Of David. The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?

**2** When evildoers assail me to eat up my flesh, my adversaries and foes, it is they who stumble and fall.

**3** Though an army encamp against me, my heart shall not fear; though war arise against me, yet I will be confident.

**4** One thing have I asked of the LORD, that will I seek after: that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to gaze upon the beauty of the LORD and to inquire in His temple.

**5** For He will hide me in His shelter in the day of trouble; He will conceal me under the cover of His tent; He will lift me high upon a rock.

**6** And now my head shall be lifted up above my enemies all around me, and I will offer in His tent sacrifices with shouts of joy; I will sing and make melody to the LORD.

**7** Hear, O LORD, when I cry aloud; be gracious to me and answer me!

**8** You have said, "Seek My face." My heart says to You, "Your face, LORD, do I seek."

**9** Hide not Your face from me. Turn not Your servant away in anger, O You who have been my help. Cast me not off; forsake me not, O God of my salvation!

**10** For my father and my mother have forsaken me, but the LORD will take me in.

**11** Teach me Your way, O LORD, and lead me on a level path because of my enemies.

**12** Give me not up to the will of my adversaries; for false witnesses have risen against me, and they breathe out violence.

**13** I believe that I shall look upon the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living!

**14** Wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the LORD!

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 27.

- **27:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **27:9** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **27:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **27:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **27:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **27:5** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **27:4**: The 'one thing' — singular focus amid plural threats. The psalmist's deepest desire is not rescue but presence.

### LOGOS
- **27:10**: One of Scripture's most tender promises: God as the parent who remains when biological parents fail. Divine adoption transcends human abandonment.

### PNEUMA
- **27:13-14**: V.13 in Hebrew begins with lulei — 'unless/if not.' The sentence structure implies: 'I would have despaired, except...' The dash before confidence creates the psalm's emotional tension.

— SOPHIA
